The main takeaway from our work is that
the chloramine dosing ratio of 3: 1 is sufficient to maintain biofilm bacterial density and bacterial functional diversity in low-nutrient GAC water.

the biofilm density on the pipe surface can be maintained at a low level (10 5 CFU / cm 2) by maintaining a residual of monochloramines at 1.5 mg / l in the drinking water, with a dosing ratio of 3 : 2 (w / w).

monochloramine at concentrations of 0.75 and 1.0 mg / L, with a 3 :1 chlorine-to-ammonia ratio, is sufficient to maintain biofilm density on pipe surfaces exposed in a GAC filter, and that the physiological profiles of the biofilm community are similar to those of biofilms grown under low-nutrient conditions.
